arxiv-2202-13274.title: OCR Improves Machine Translation for Low-Resource Languages
arxiv-2202-13274.creator: Oana Ignat, Jean Maillard, Vishrav Chaudhary, Francisco Guzmán, University of Michigan, Meta AI, Microsoft Turing
arxiv-2202-13274.description: Abstract We aim to investigate the performance of current OCR systems on low resource languages and low resource scripts. We introduce and make publicly available a novel benchmark, OCR4MT , consisting of real and synthetic data, enriched with noise, for 60 low-resource languages in low resource scripts. We evaluate state-of-the-art OCR systems on our benchmark and analyse most common errors.

arxiv-2409-15857.title: Large-scale Benchmarks for Multimodal Recommendation with Ducho
arxiv-2409-15857.creator: Matteo Attimonelli, Danilo Danese, Angela Di Fazio, Daniele Malitesta, Claudio Pomo, Tommaso Di Noia
arxiv-2409-15857.description: Abstract With the advent of deep learning and, more recently, large models, recommendation systems have greatly refined their capability of profiling users’ preferences and interests that, in most cases, are complex to disentangle. This is especially true for those recommendation algorithms that rely heavily on external side information, such as multimodal recommender systems.

arxiv-2501-17995.title: Simulating the photospheric to coronal plasma using magnetohydrodyanamic characteristics II: reflections on non-reflecting boundary conditions Correctness of the MHD eigensystem was verified using Mathematica ( Wolfram Research 2019 ) . The primary 3D MHD code, LaRe3D v.2.10 ( Arber et al. 2001 ) ,
arxiv-2501-17995.creator: N. Dylan Kee, Lucas A. Tarr, Peter W. Schuck, Mark G. Linton, James E. Leake
arxiv-2501-17995.description: Abstract We present our implementation of non-reflecting boundary conditions in the magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) code LaRe3D . This implementation couples a characteristics-based boundary condition with a Lagrangian remap code, demonstrating the generality and flexibility of such non-reflecting boundary conditions for use with arbitrary grid-based MHD schemes.

arxiv-2503-17562.title: Sequential HW-Aware Precoding: Over-the-air cancellation of HWI in Downlink Cell-Free Massive MIMO with Serial Fronthaul
arxiv-2503-17562.creator: Antoine Durant, Asma Mabrouk, and Rafik Zayani
arxiv-2503-17562.description: Abstract This paper addresses the critical challenge of mitigating hardware impairments (HWIs) in downlink cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) networks while ensuring computational scalability. We propose a novel sequential hardware-aware (HW-aware) precoding technique that leverages the serial fronthaul topology to perform over-the-air HWI cancellation.

arxiv-2506-09793.title: A matheuristic for solving the single row facility layout problem
arxiv-2506-09793.creator: Thomas Pammer, Markus Sinnl
arxiv-2506-09793.description: Abstract The single row facility layout problem (SRFLP) is a well-studied NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem with applications in manufacturing and logistics systems. In the SRFLP, a set of facilities with lengths is given, as well as weights between each pair of facilities.

arxiv-2506-19626.title: Scaling Up Unbiased Search-based Symbolic Regression
arxiv-2506-19626.creator: Paul Kahlmeyer, Joachim Giesen, Michael Habeck, Henrik Voigt
arxiv-2506-19626.description: Abstract In a regression task, a function is learned from labeled data to predict the labels at new data points. The goal is to achieve small prediction errors. In symbolic regression, the goal is more ambitious, namely, to learn an interpretable function that makes small prediction errors.

pmc-11490915.title: Prevalence and associated factors of post-traumatic stress symptoms in hospitalised children with cancer and their parents in South China: A multicentred cross-sectional study
pmc-11490915.creator: Yunyun Peng, Lin Xu, Can Gu, Guiyuan Ma, Zitong Zhang, Yilin Zhang, Li Liu, Jianhui Xie, Sulan Lin, Stanley Kam Ki Lam
pmc-11490915.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to examine the prevalence and risk factors of Post-Traumatic Stress Symptoms (PTSS) in hospitalised children with cancer and their parents and explore the PTSS correlation between parents and children.MethodsData were collected using the University of California at Los Angeles (UCLA) Posttraumatic Stress Disorder-Reaction Index for DSM-IV and the Chinese version of the Impact of Event Scale-Revised Questionnaire.

pmc-11503404.title: Cardiomyopathies: The Role of Non-Coding RNAs
pmc-11503404.creator: Nicole Carabetta, Chiara Siracusa, Isabella Leo, Giuseppe Panuccio, Antonio Strangio, Jolanda Sabatino, Daniele Torella, Salvatore De Rosa, Francisco J Enguita, Gaetano Santulli
pmc-11503404.description: Cardiomyopathies are the structural and functional disorders of the myocardium. Etiopathogenesis is complex and involves an interplay of genetic, environmental, and lifestyle factors eventually leading to myocardial abnormalities. It is known that non-coding (Nc) RNAs, including micro (mi)-RNAs and long non-coding (lnc) RNAs, play a crucial role in regulating gene expression.

pmc-11680413.title: Vitamins, Minerals and Phytonutrients as Modulators of Canine Immune Function: A Literature Review
pmc-11680413.creator: Carolina Barroso, António J M Fonseca, Ana R J Cabrita, Guillermo Tellez-Isaias
pmc-11680413.description: Simple SummaryAs pets are increasingly seen as family members, there is a growing interest in incorporating functional supplements into pet food to improve animal health. Several commercial dog diets claim to support normal immune system function, but scientific evidence is limited.

pmc-11711957.title: Building a dementia care effectiveness trial to facilitate and anticipate widespread intervention adoption
pmc-11711957.creator: Richard H Fortinsky, Julie T Robison
pmc-11711957.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThis presentation maps the journey of an evidence‐based dementia care program from effectiveness trial design to adoption by policymakers as an ongoing program available to eligible older adults living at home with dementia and their care partners. Care of People with Dementia in their Environments (COPE) is a non‐pharmacologic program that seeks to maximize physical function and quality of life in people with dementia and build dementia management skills in care partners.

pmc-12505809.title: Prevalence of substance use disorder in individuals with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder: associations with sex and psychiatric comorbidity
pmc-12505809.creator: Camilla Djønne Moldekleiv, Astri J Lundervold, Berit Skretting Solberg, Anders Engeland, Lars Thore Fadnes, Fatemeh Chalabianloo, Kari Klungsøyr
pmc-12505809.description: BackgroundSeveral studies have reported associations between attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and substance use disorders (SUD). However, sex-differences in ADHD and SUD, especially when associated with other psychiatric comorbidities, are less studied.ObjectiveTo compare the prevalence of SUD among individuals with and without ADHD to describe groups, defined by sex and psychiatric comorbidity, who may benefit from targeted follow-up.

pmc-12511134.title: The efficacy and safety of extended thromboprophylaxis after colorectal surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12511134.creator: Joseph Do Woong Choi, Nguyen Huynh, Talia Shepherd, Aswin Shanmugalingam, Fiona Lee Gavegan, Karen Shedden, Amy Cao, Nimalan Pathmanathan, Toufic El-Khoury, Kerry Hitos, James Wei Tatt Toh
pmc-12511134.description: PurposeTo report (1) efficacy and (2) safety outcomes comparing extended thromboprophylaxis (ETP) with low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) versus no ETP after colorectal surgery.MethodsA systematic review using MEDLINE, EMBASE and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials to March 2024.

pmc-12574052.title: Lifestyle changes and postmenopausal breast cancer risk in women from the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition
pmc-12574052.creator: Fanélie Vasson, Komodo Matta, Carine Biessy, Christian S Antoniussen, Agnès Fournier, Chloé Marques, Claire Cadeau, Charlotte Le Cornet, Renée T Fortner, Matthias B Schulze, Sabina Sieri, Salvatore Panico, Rosario Tumino, Fulvio Ricceri, Giovanna Masala, Anouk E Hiensch, Evelyn M Monninkhof, Antonio
pmc-12574052.description: BackgroundThe risk of breast cancer has been associated with various lifestyle factors, yet the evidence regarding how lifestyle modifications affect this risk remains limited. This study examines the relationship between changes in the Healthy Lifestyle Index (HLI) and postmenopausal breast cancer risk in women participating in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer (EPIC).

pmc-12603529.title: Identification of risk factors for malnutrition in patients with severe pneumonia and development of a predictive model to guide personalized enteral nutrition care
pmc-12603529.creator: Fang Yang, Peibei Zhang, Hongyi Sun, Qingye Zhang
pmc-12603529.description: BackgroundMalnutrition is a frequent complication in patients with severe pneumonia, contributing to impaired immune function, delayed recovery, and increased morbidity and mortality. Early identification of patients at risk is critical for implementing timely nutritional support. However, evidence regarding the risk factors for malnutrition in severe pneumonia remains limited, and no predictive tools are currently available to guide individualized nutritional care.

pmc-13145134.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A2108 STROKE UNIT ASSESMENT OF BLOOD PRESSURE IN SPONTANEOUS INTRACEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE: STABLE STUDY
pmc-13145134.creator: Diego Villagran Sancho, Carlota Villar Rodriguez, Luis Fernández Espigares, Luis Manzano-Hernández, Manuel Medina-Rodriguez, Andrés Hermosín-Gómez, Elena Zapata Arriaza, Juan Antonio Cabezas Rodriguez, Francisco Moniche
pmc-13145134.description: Background and aimsEarly initiation of blood pressure (BP)-lowering treatment and BP control are associated with improved functional outcomes in intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Our aim was to analyze BP management strategies and identify factors that might influence its control.MethodsProspective observational study of patients with spontaneous ICH (sICH) evaluating time metrics and rate of BP control at hospital admission.

pmc-13382762.title: Cyclic Mechanical Deformation of Denture PMMA Regulates Fungal Biofilm Virulence
pmc-13382762.creator: Carolina Montoya, Ryan Yu-Sheng Chang, Dmitriy A. Dikin, Mike Sousanieh, Zhenting Xiang, Yuan Liu, Sumant Puri, Santiago Orrego
pmc-13382762.description: Cyclic mechanical deformation is a well-characterized phenomenon in polymeric biomaterials under physiological mastication loading, yet its role in regulating biological responses at material interfaces remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate whether cyclic mechanical loading of denture-base poly­(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) functions as a biomaterial-derived cue that regulates fungal biofilm behavior.

pmc-13447935.title: An end-to-end deep learning framework with nonstationary weighting strategy for enhancing reservoir landslide displacement prediction
pmc-13447935.creator: Ningxin Weng, Lei Fan, Lihuang Tang
pmc-13447935.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Accurate prediction of temporal reservoir landslide displacement using key environmental variables, such as rainfall depth, reservoir water level, and groundwater level, is crucial for early warning. These variables exhibit distinct, time-varying influences on displacement, yet conventional deep learning models often overlook such dynamics by adopting stationary sliding windows and assigning equal importance to all variables and timesteps, thereby limiting forecasting accuracy.
